question: Which athlete won the gold medal in the Men's Javelin Throw F46 category at the Para Athletics World Championships 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sumit Antil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sumit Antil won the gold medal in the Men's Javelin Throw F46 category at the **Para Athletics World Championships 2023**.
 
• He set a championship record with a throw of **70.83 meters**, showcasing his dominance in the event.
 
• Sumit Antil is a Paralympic champion, having also won gold at the **Tokyo Paralympics 2020** in the same category.
 
• His performance at the Para Athletics World Championships 2023 further solidifies his status as one of the best para-athletes globally.
 
• F46 category is designated for athletes with upper limb impairments, and Sumit continues to inspire millions with his exceptional achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Para Athletics World Championships:**

 
 
• A biennial event organized by the World Para Athletics, featuring athletes with various physical disabilities.
 
• The 2023 edition was held in **Paris, France**, serving as a qualifying event for the Paris 2024 Paralympics.
 
• The competition includes track and field events across multiple classifications based on the type and severity of the disability.
 
 
 
• **F46 Classification:**
 
 
• The F46 category is for athletes with upper limb impairments, such as amputation or restricted range of motion.
 
• It allows athletes to compete on a level playing field by grouping participants with similar levels of ability.
 
 
 
• **Sumit Antil's Achievements:**
 
 
• Gold medalist at the **Tokyo Paralympics 2020** in the Men's Javelin Throw F46 category.
 
• Holder of multiple world records in the F46 category, including a throw of **68.55 meters** at the Tokyo Paralympics.
 
 
 
• **India at Para Athletics:**
 
 
• India has been making significant strides in para-athletics, with athletes like Sumit Antil, Devendra Jhajharia, and Mariyappan Thangavelu achieving global recognition.
 
• These achievements reflect the growing support and infrastructure for para-sports in India.
